Você agora escolhe o tempo pela ideia, e: You now choose tenses by the idea, not by memory: finished and dated (preterite), background or habit (imperfect), linked to the present (present perfect), before another past event (pluperfect), a plan or a guess (future), politeness or a hypothesis (conditional, subjunctive). Reveja a aula 60. Diga uma frase com «a»: Review lesson 60. Say one sentence with the personal «a», one with a verb + preposition and one with an attached pronoun.
PASSO 1: pergunte primeiro: a ação termi: STEP 1: ask first: is the action finished and do I place it at a definite time (ayer, el año pasado, en 2019)? Then use the preterite: «Ayer compré pan», «Nació en 2001». STEP 2: is the action a past habit, a description, a setting or something in progress? Use the imperfect: «Cuando era niño, iba a la playa cada verano», «Llovía y hacía frío». This is the trap for English speakers: English "I used to go" and "I WOULD go every summer" (habit) are both the imperfect «iba», never the conditional «iría»; and "I was walking" is «caminaba». STEP 3: is the action linked to the present or to a period that isn't over (hoy, esta semana, este año, nunca, ya, todavía)? In Spain, use the present perfect: «Hoy he trabajado mucho», «Nunca he estado en Perú». STEP 4: did the action happen before another past moment? Use the pluperfect: «Cuando llegué, el tren ya había salido» (the train had already left). STEP 5: in a story, the imperfect describes the background and the preterite narrates the events: «Mientras caminaba por la calle, vi a un amigo» (While I was walking down the street, I saw a friend). Both fit in one sentence: the imperfect is what was going on; the preterite is what interrupted it. STEP 6: IMPORTANT, varieties: in most of Latin America the preterite replaces the present perfect for recent actions: «Hoy comí temprano», and the perfect is less frequent — much like American English "I already ate". In Spain the distinction is sharper. In both varieties, «ayer», «anoche» and «el año pasado» take the preterite. STEP 7: remember the irregular preterites: fui (ir and ser), hice, dije, tuve, estuve, pude, puse, supe, quise, vine, di, vi, traje. And the imperfect has only three irregulars: ser (era), ir (iba) and ver (veía).
em português, o pretérito perfeito simpl: English "When I was a kid, I would go to the beach every summer" uses "would" for a habit, but Spanish uses the imperfect: «iba», not «iría». English "was -ing" for an action in progress is also the imperfect: «caminaba». And as in British English, with «ayer» you can't use the present perfect: «Ayer compré», never «Ayer he comprado».
Yesterday I bought bread at the bakery.

PASSO 1: o futuro simples (-é, -ás, -á,: STEP 1: the simple future (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án) is added to the infinitive: «hablaré», «comerás», «vivirá». Common irregulars: tendré, podré, haré, diré, pondré, saldré, vendré, querré, sabré, habré. STEP 2: the future also expresses probability in the present: «Ahora estará en casa» (He must be at home now / I suppose he's at home). And the future perfect expresses probability in the past: «Habrá salido ya» (He must have left already). STEP 3: the conditional (-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían) uses the same irregular stems: «tendría», «podría», «haría». It's used for politeness («¿Podría ayudarme?»), advice («Deberías descansar» — You should rest), the future seen from the past («Dijo que vendría» — He said he would come) and hypotheses. STEP 4: the conditional perfect (habría + past participle) expresses what would have happened: «Habría ido, pero estaba enfermo» (I would have gone, but I was ill). STEP 5: «si» hypotheses come in three types. If it's possible: «Si llueve, me quedo en casa» or «me quedaré» (si + present, no future after «si»). If it's unlikely or unreal in the present: «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría» (si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional). If it's unreal in the past: «Si hubiera sabido, habría venido» (si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect). STEP 6: never use the conditional or the future right after «si» in hypotheses. STEP 7: «quizá», «tal vez» and «posiblemente» take the subjunctive when there's doubt: «Quizá venga»; «a lo mejor» always takes the indicative: «A lo mejor viene».
em português, o futuro do pretérito («fa: English "If I had money, I would travel" maps neatly onto «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría». The typical mistake comes from colloquial English "if I would have known": in Spanish the conditional never goes after «si» («si habría sabido» is wrong) — it's «si hubiera sabido, habría venido». And English "He must be at home" (a guess) is the future: «Estará en casa».
He must be at home now.
He said he would come on Monday.
If it rains, I'll stay at home.
If I had money, I would travel.
If I had known, I would have come.
Depois de «si», o verbo vai ao imperfect: After «si», the verb goes into the imperfect subjunctive, not the conditional.

Imperfecto de subjuntivo pede condiciona: The imperfect subjunctive calls for the conditional in the other clause.

PASSO 1: use o subjuntivo depois de dese: STEP 1: use the subjunctive after wishes, orders or requests («quiero que vengas» — I want you to come), doubt («dudo que sea verdad»), emotion («me alegro de que estés aquí») and negative opinion («no creo que llueva»). STEP 2: use the subjunctive after «cuando» when talking about the future: «Cuando llegues, llámame» (When you arrive, call me). For habits or past facts, use the indicative: «Cuando llego, saludo». STEP 3: «para que», «antes de que», «sin que» and «a no ser que» always take the subjunctive: «Te lo explico para que lo entiendas». STEP 4: «aunque» + indicative gives a fact: «Aunque hace calor, salgo» (Although it's hot, I'm going out); + subjunctive gives a hypothesis or something that doesn't matter: «Aunque haga calor, saldré» (Even if it's hot, I'll go out). STEP 5: sequence of tenses: with a main verb in the present or future, the subjunctive is present or perfect: «Quiero que vengas», «Espero que hayas llegado bien». With a main verb in the past, the subjunctive is imperfect: «Quería que vinieras», «Me pidió que le ayudara». STEP 6: «ojalá» + present subjunctive = a possible wish («Ojalá venga»); «ojalá» + imperfect = an unlikely wish («Ojalá tuviera más tiempo» — I wish I had more time).
em português também usamos o subjuntivo: English "I want you to come" uses an infinitive; Spanish uses «que» + subjunctive: «Quiero que vengas». English "when you arrive" uses the present for the future; Spanish uses the present subjunctive: «cuando llegues» — not the indicative «cuando llegas», and never the future «cuando llegarás». English "I wish I had…" = «Ojalá tuviera…».
Para o futuro depois de «cuando», o espa: For the future after «cuando», Spanish uses the subjunctive.
Verbo principal no passado pede imperfec: A main verb in the past takes the imperfect subjunctive.
Una carta desde Valencia / Uma carta de: Una carta desde Valencia / A letter from Valencia
Querida Marta: Escrevo de Valência, onde: Dear Marta, I'm writing from Valencia, where I arrived on Monday. When I was little, I always dreamt of living by the sea, and now I'm doing it. Before coming, I'd been looking for a flat for weeks, but I couldn't find anything cheap. In the end I found one near the beach. If I'd waited another month, I'd probably have lost it. The landlord told me that, when the course ends, I'll be able to stay another year. I hope you come and see me in the summer; I'll show you the city and, even if it's hot, we'll go to the beach. I doubt my flat is very big, but there'll be a bed for you. Write soon. Love, Lucía.
